title: Write ooRexx; if Python is truly needed, say why in PYTHON_JUSTIFICATION
summary: packages/oorexx_python_gate_v0.1 (Claude (Opus 5.5); architecture Tom Dyer) fails any estate package that carries Python, or calls Python, without saying why ooRexx can't do the job. It is written in ooRexx and logs through oorexx_logging. Autobuild v0.5.3 runs it first on every package, as test 01 (python-justification-gate). The reason for it: asked to read a file, a model reaches for Python, wraps it in two lines of Rexx, and calls the result ooRexx. Arguing about it chat by chat has not stopped that; a build gate does.
invariants: Every Python file, and every file that calls Python, needs a line in PYTHON_JUSTIFICATION at the package root: 'path | reason', with at least 10 words of reason.
The gate cannot judge a reason; it prints every reason in the build log, so the VERIFIER and the Architect can.
'Reading a file is complex' is not a reason: the estate has ooRexx libraries for formats, archives and cryptography.
procedure: If it fails, rewrite the Python in ooRexx, or add a justification a reviewer would accept.
